html:
A joint statement signed in Abu Dhabi on 4 February 2019 by Pope Francis and Ahmed el-Tayeb, the Grand Imam of al-Azhar, the leading seat of Sunni learning in Cairo. It calls on Christians, Muslims and all people to live together in peace.

It grew out of years of talks between the two men. The document condemns killing in the name of God, terrorism and the use of religion to stir hatred. It defends freedom of belief, the rights of women and children, and full citizenship for religious minorities, and it calls on world leaders to work for peace.

Francis's trip was the first by a pope to the Arabian Peninsula, and he held a large open-air Mass for migrant workers in Abu Dhabi. The United Arab Emirates used the occasion to present itself as a land of tolerance. The UN later made 4 February the International Day of Human Fraternity, and a mosque, church and synagogue were built side by side in Abu Dhabi, opening in 2023. The statement echoes the Jordanian Amman Message of 2004.
